#: citare's supplement to reporters-db's reporters.json, applied by crates/citare-core/build.rs.
Each editions entry names one edition by its reporters.json key (reporter), its cluster's name, and its edition name, and replaces that edition's regexes and, when it gives start or end, that date.

Each reporters entry adds a reporter reporters-db doesn't have under its reporters.json key, as a cluster of its own with one edition; reporters-db may have the same books under another key, which then shares the slug (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS).
Each variations entry adds another abbreviation (variation) for one edition, named like an editions or reporters entry, that matches only through the entry's own regexes.

Each journals entry adds a secondary source journals.json doesn't have, such as an encyclopedia, to the journals under its abbreviation (edition), so a citation of it is a journal citation even when a reporter has the same abbreviation.

examples: citations the entry must recognize as that edition, with the volume each must have; rejects: citations it must no longer recognize as that edition. crates/citare-core/tests/reporters_local.rs checks both.

editions.name: Ohio Reports
editions.notes: The Ohio Reports (1821-1851) have 20 volumes, CAP's `ohio` (vols 1-20). reporters-db takes any one- to three-digit volume, so `127 Ohio 545`, the Ohio State Reports cited as `Ohio`, took the Ohio Reports' slug (#80). The variations entry below gives it to the Ohio State Reports. A closed series, so the cap says a volume past 20 isn't the Ohio Reports (docs/volume-caps.md): the Ohio Reports ran 1821-1851 (Cardiff Index to Legal Abbreviations, https://www.legalabbrevs.cardiff.ac.uk/titles/tview/id/4397/tsearch//ttype/Exact) and the Ohio State Reports began again at volume 1 in 1852 (1 Ohio St., https://cite.case.law/ohio-st/1/).

editions.name: Iowa Reports, Bradford
editions.notes: Iowa's Bradford (1839-1841) has three volumes, CAP's `bradf`. reporters-db takes any volume, so `4 Bradf. 268`, Bradford's Surrogate Reports (CAP's `brad`, vols 1-4) cited as `Bradf.`, took Iowa's slug (#99). The reporters entry for `Bradf.` below adds Bradford's Surrogate Reports under the same abbreviation, which a citation without a year in Iowa's run takes first (citare_data_build::slugs::SORTS_LAST). The cap of three volumes is CAP's holdings only (`bradf`, vols 1-3): I found no source outside CAP for the series' last volume (docs/volume-caps.md). A volume past 3 is Bradford's Surrogate Reports, so the cap loses no citation.

editions.name: Caines' Reports
editions.notes: reporters-db's entry for Caines' Reports, CAP's `cai` (vols 1-3), which the reporters entry `Cai.` below adds under CAP's short name. It shares `cai` with that entry (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS, D78), replacing the released slug `cai-r`, which named no CAP volume. reporters-db takes any volume; this takes Caines' Reports' three, with the regexes of `Cai.`. The series closed at three volumes: 'Caine's reports, 3 v.' in the contents of the New York Common Law Reports (https://archive.org/details/reportsofcasesad04newyiala; docs/volume-caps.md).

editions.name: Puerto Rico Reports
editions.notes: reporters-db's entry for the Puerto Rico Reports, CAP's `pr` (vols 3-100), which the reporters entry `P.R.` below adds under CAP's short name. It shares `pr` with that entry (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS, D78), replacing the released slug `p-r-r`, which named no CAP volume. reporters-db takes any volume; this takes the series' 100, as `P.R.` does, so `101 P.R.R. 1` is no longer a citation. The series closed at volume 100: v. 3 (1899) to v. 100 (1972), vols 1-2 published in Spanish only (Berkeley Law catalogue, https://lawcat.berkeley.edu/record/183605; Washington State Law Library, https://lawlibrary.courts.wa.gov/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=13950; docs/volume-caps.md).

editions.name: Connecticut Superior Court Reports
editions.notes: The Reports ran 1986-1994 in a handful of volumes. reporters-db takes any volume, which also matches the Superior Court's neutral citation (`1999 Conn. Super. Ct. 13301-M`, volume a year); capping the volume at three digits lets the two share `conn-super-ct`. A disambiguation cap, not a last volume (docs/volume-caps.md): it says only that a four-digit volume is the neutral citation's year, and the year written as the volume is what decides.

editions.name: Reports of Massachusetts Appellate Division
editions.notes: The numbered series (CAP's `mass-app-div`, vols 1-15). reporters-db takes any volume, which also matches the annual series added below (`1995 Mass. App. Div. 12`, volume a year); capping the volume at three digits tells the two apart. A disambiguation cap, not a last volume (docs/volume-caps.md): it says only that a four-digit volume is the annual series' year, and the year written as the volume is what decides.

editions.name: Pennsylvania Fiduciary Reporter
editions.notes: CAP's `pa-fid` (one volume, 'Pa. Fid.', published 1981 by Geo. T. Bisel, cases 1977-1981) is volume 1 of the Fiduciary Reporter's second series (`Fid. Rep. 2d`): all 12 citations of `1 Fid. Rep. 2d` in the CAP opinions measured (docs/reporters-local.md), written six ways, give the first page of the CAP case of the same name (`Lieberman Estate, 1 Fid. Rep. 2d 281`, CAP pa-fid/1 0281-01). reporters-db's dates (1977-1981) are that one volume's; the second series ran from v. 1 (1981) to v. 30 (2010) (https://encore.jenkinslaw.org/iii/encore/record/C__Rb111056; https://lawcat.berkeley.edu/record/281833), so the edition takes volumes 1 to 30 and ends in 2010 (D82). No opinion measured writes `Pa. Fid.`; it is CAP's form, and `Fid. Rep. 2d` shares its slug.

reporters.name: Reports of Massachusetts Appellate Division (Annual)
reporters.notes: The annual series, whose volume is its year: CAP's `mass-app-div-annual` (vols 1980-2015, 'Reports of Massachusetts Appellate Division (Annual)'). reporters-db lists only the one `Mass. App. Div.`, so without this entry a citation to an annual volume took the numbered series' slug, `mass-app-div` (#75).

reporters.name: Bradford's Surrogate Reports (N.Y.)
reporters.notes: CAP's `brad` (vols 1-4, 'Bradford's Reports'), New York Surrogate's Court decisions of 1849-1857, whose cases CAP cites as `1 Brad. 1`. reporters-db has `Brad.` only as a variation of Iowa's Bradford (`bradf`), so CAP's own citations took Iowa's slug (#99). Of the 114 `Brad.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case, 113 name a case in `brad` and one in `bradf`. The series closed at four volumes, cases of 1849-1857 (HathiTrust, https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008916078; docs/volume-caps.md).

reporters.name: Bradford's Surrogate Reports (N.Y.)
reporters.notes: Bradford's Surrogate Reports (CAP's `brad`, vols 1-4) under the abbreviation New York opinions cite them by most, `Bradf.`, which reporters-db gives only Iowa's Bradford (`bradf`). Its slug is `brad` (citare_data_build::slugs::BY_REPORTER), and Iowa's `Bradf.` sorts after it (SORTS_LAST), so `1 Bradf. 356` is `brad` and `1 Bradf. 3 (1840)` is `bradf`. Its regex for volumes 1 to 3 is Iowa's, so one extractor finds both editions in that order; with two extractors the first one's edition would come first. Of the 793 `Bradf.` citations of volumes 1 to 4 in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md), none is Iowa's Bradford: CAP resolves 610 to `brad` and 14 to `bradf`, and those 14 are New York opinions citing a New York surrogate's case at a page Iowa's volume also has (`Weir v. Fitzgerald, 2 Bradf. 42`). Iowa's opinions cite Iowa's Bradford without a volume (`Bradford, 16`, 58 times) and every `Bradf.` or `Brad.` with a volume in them is the New York reports (#99, D73). The series closed at four volumes, cases of 1849-1857 (HathiTrust, https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008916078; docs/volume-caps.md).

reporters.name: Caines' Reports
reporters.notes: CAP's `cai` (vols 1-3), Caines' Reports of the New York Supreme Court of Judicature, 1803-1805, whose cases CAP cites as `1 Cai. 1`. reporters-db has the reporter as `Cai. R.` (released as `cai-r`, now `cai`) and `Cai.` as a variation of Caines' Cases (`cai-cas`), so `1 Cai. 1` took Caines' Cases' slug (#99). Of the 117 `Cai.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case in either reporter, 114 name a case in `cai` and 3 in `cai-cas`; the Bluebook (T1) also gives `Cai.` to Caines' Reports and `Cai. Cas.` to Caines' Cases. reporters-db's `Cai. R.` shares `cai` (D78). The series closed at three volumes: 'Caine's reports, 3 v.' in the contents of the New York Common Law Reports (https://archive.org/details/reportsofcasesad04newyiala; docs/volume-caps.md).

reporters.name: T.U.P. Charlton's Reports (Ga.)
reporters.notes: CAP's `charlton-rep` (vol 1, 'Charlton's Reports'), T.U.P. Charlton's reports of Georgia superior court decisions from 1805 to 1824, whose cases CAP cites as `1 Charlton Rep. 13`. reporters-db has only R.M. Charlton's reports (1811-1837, CAP's `charlton`, cited `1 Charlton 1`), with `Charlton Rep.` as one of its variations, so CAP's citations of T.U.P. Charlton took R.M. Charlton's slug (#99). Georgia opinions write `T. U. P. Charlton, 311` without a volume, which no reporter regex reads; `Charlton Rep.` is CAP's own form. One volume, published 1824 (VIAF, https://viaf.org/viaf/53766484; Cardiff Index to Legal Abbreviations, https://www.legalabbrevs.cardiff.ac.uk/titles/view/id/4942; docs/volume-caps.md).

reporters.name: New Mexico Appellate Reports
reporters.notes: CAP's `nm-app` (vols 1-10, 2011-2016), which reporters-db doesn't have (#99). CAP cites every case in it by its neutral citation (`2011-NMCA-108`, `2016-NMSC-021`), and no opinion in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) cites `N.M. App.`; the edition gives CAP's slug a name and reads the citation if one is written. It takes any volume: the series is still published as unofficial hardbound volumes (UNM Law Library, https://libguides.law.unm.edu/c.php?g=244202&p=2316952; Rule 23-112 NMRA), so CAP's ten volumes are not its last (docs/volume-caps.md, D80). New Mexico opinions also write a Court of Appeals case in the New Mexico Reports with the court in the reporter, `84 N.M.App. 83` (CAP nm/84); the variations entry for `N.M.` below takes that form, and the edition's start year tells the two apart.

reporters.name: Puerto Rico Reports
reporters.notes: CAP's `pr` (vols 3-100), the English Puerto Rico Reports, whose cases CAP cites as `3 P.R. 2`. reporters-db has the reporter as `P.R.R.` (released as `p-r-r`, now `pr`) and `P.R.` as a variation of it, the Pacific Reporter and Penrose and Watts, so `45 P.R. 100` was ambiguous and took the Pacific Reporter's slug `p` (#99). All 85 `P.R.` and `P. R.` citations in the CAP case metadata measured (docs/reporters-local.md) that CAP resolves to a case name one in `pr`. Its own opinions write `P.R.R.` (30,866 times in `pr`), reporters-db's entry, which shares `pr` (D78). The series closed at volume 100: v. 3 (1899) to v. 100 (1972), vols 1-2 published in Spanish only (Berkeley Law catalogue, https://lawcat.berkeley.edu/record/183605; Washington State Law Library, https://lawlibrary.courts.wa.gov/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=13950; docs/volume-caps.md). The 1,239 CourtListener citations written `P.R.` of vols 168-193 (2006-2015) are the Decisiones de Puerto Rico, a different reporter (citare#108).

reporters.name: Fiduciary Reporter (Pa.)
reporters.notes: The Fiduciary Reporter's first series (Geo. T. Bisel; selected Pennsylvania orphans' court decisions), vol. 1 (1951) to v. 30 (1980) (https://encore.jenkinslaw.org/iii/encore/record/C__Rb111056; https://lawcat.berkeley.edu/record/281833), which CAP doesn't have. Opinions cite vol. 1 cases decided as early as 1947 (`Kyle Estate, 1 Fiduc. Rep. 131 (1947)`, CAP pa-d-c2d/29/0464-01), hence the 1947 start. reporters-db has no entry for it (D82). Courts write it most often `Fiduc. Rep.`; the variations entries add the forms counted in docs/reporters-local.md.

reporters.name: Fiduciary Reporter, Second Series (Pa.)
reporters.notes: The Fiduciary Reporter's second series, 2nd ser., v. 1 (1981) to v. 30 (2010) (https://encore.jenkinslaw.org/iii/encore/record/C__Rb111056; https://lawcat.berkeley.edu/record/281833), abbreviated `Fid.Rep.2d` and `Pa.Fiduc.2d` in Jenkins Law Library's record. Volume 1, with cases decided 1977-1981, is CAP's `pa-fid`, which CAP and reporters-db call `Pa. Fid.`; the two share that slug (citare_data_build::slugs::SAME_BOOKS). The last volume has 2010 decisions (`Pendergrass Will, 30 Fid.Rep.2d 430 (Montgomery O.C. 2010)`, https://resources.evans-legal.com/?p=4501) (D82).

reporters.name: Fiduciary Reporter, Third Series (Pa.)
reporters.notes: The Fiduciary Reporter's third series, 3rd ser., v. 1 (2011) to v. 13 (2022), followed by the fourth series in 2023 (https://encore.jenkinslaw.org/iii/encore/record/C__Rb111056, which gives the abbreviations `Fid.Rep.3d` and `Pa.Fiduc.3d`). `Cassalia Trusts, 12 Fid.Rep.3d 562 (Montgomery O.C. 2022)` (https://resources.evans-legal.com/?p=9630) (D82).

reporters.name: Fiduciary Reporter, Fourth Series (Pa.)
reporters.notes: The Fiduciary Reporter's fourth series, 4th ser., v. 1 (2023)- (https://encore.jenkinslaw.org/iii/encore/record/C__Rb111056), still published, so it takes any volume (docs/volume-caps.md). Volume 1 reports 2022 decisions (`Dembosky Estate, 1 Fid.Rep.4th 267 (Lackawanna O.C. 2022)`, https://resources.evans-legal.com/?p=10351), hence the 2022 start. The catalogue abbreviates it `Fid.Rep.4d` and `Pa.Fiduc.4d`; opinions and practitioners write `Fid.Rep.4th` (D82).

variations.name: New Mexico Reports
variations.notes: New Mexico opinions write a Court of Appeals case in the New Mexico Reports (CAP's `nm`) with the court in the reporter: `84 N.M.App. 83` (CAP nm/84). The New Mexico Appellate Reports (`N.M. App.`, CAP's `nm-app`) begin in 2011, and the regex is theirs, so one extractor finds both editions: a citation with a year before 2011 is the New Mexico Reports and one with a later year or none is the New Mexico Appellate Reports (crates/citare-core/src/helpers.rs guess_edition; docs/volume-caps.md, D80).

variations.name: Ohio State Reports
variations.notes: Older opinions, most often Illinois and Indiana ones, cite the Ohio State Reports (1852-1964, CAP's `ohio-st`, vols 1-177) as `Ohio`. A volume of 21 to 177 can't be the Ohio Reports, which end at volume 20; of 142 such citations in CAP's case metadata for Ohio, Illinois, Indiana and Massachusetts courts and N.E.2d vols 1-250, 103 name the first page of an Ohio State Reports case and 37 a page inside one (#80). Volumes 1 to 20 stay the Ohio Reports, which they are far more often. The cap at 177 is the Ohio State Reports' last volume (1964; the Ohio State Reports, Second Series, begin at volume 1 in 1965), from the University of Akron's case citation guide (https://libguides.uakron.edu/LARW/casecitations); it gates only the spelling `Ohio`, not the Ohio State Reports (docs/volume-caps.md).

journals.name: American Jurisprudence
journals.notes: reporters-db's only `Am. Jur.` is the American Jurist and Law Magazine (1829-1843, 28 volumes). Opinions after the 1930s cite American Jurisprudence, the encyclopedia (first series 1936-1948, 58 volumes), as `Am. Jur.`: `Smith v. United States ex rel. Gorlo, 7 Cir., 52 F.2d 848; 13 Am.Jur. 383` in CAP a2d/31/0693-01 (#93). Both are secondary sources, so a citation of `Am. Jur.` is a journal citation; a year in the American Jurist's run picks it, and otherwise the citation is the encyclopedia.
